excerpt: necessity: if [p] is (fully) grounded in D, then ☐(∧D → p). With these two principles in place, the argument for necessity is as follows: (1) Suppose that [p] is (fully) grounded in D. (2) By (1) and significance, the connecting question ‘Why should [p] obtain given that each member of D obtains?’ lacks cognitive significance. (3) By (2) and essence, there are essential truths about [p], D, the plurality consisting of [p] and D, or the entities they involve according to which ∧D → p. (4) The essential truths are metaphysically necessary. (5) By (3) and (4), ☐(∧D → p).
overview: This is the paper’s central formal argument. It connects full grounding to the absence of cognitive significance, then to essential truths, and finally to metaphysical necessity. Its scope is restricted to full grounds and to the proposition corresponding to what is grounded, not to stronger claims that grounding itself must recur in every possible world.
title: Necessity Argument Outline
